thread:
cheng: Hey infra team — can we spin up a small GPU node pool in ap-southeast-3 for batch embedding jobs? Low steady QPS, bursty at night. Need guidance on instance type (A10G vs T4), autoscaler min/max, taints/tolerations, and NAT/egress IP constraints. I want 8 concurrent pods max initially.

alex: +1 on the ask. For batch embeddings latency isn't critical so T4 is cheaper but A10G gives much better throughput per GPU. If jobs can pack many requests per GPU, A10G might reduce node count.

sam: Agree. If cost is primary -> T4. If throughput per node matters -> A10G. Also consider single-GPU nodes to keep packing/simple scheduling.

maria: Ops notes: our ap-southeast-3 subnet only has 2 spare NAT IPs left. If we create a new nodepool that spawns many nodes with ephemeral external IPs it's going to blow the pool. Recommend using Cloud NAT or ensure nodes have no external IPs (private nodes) plus NAT gateway scaled for burst.

ops-oncall: FYI we've hit the Cloud NAT TCP ephemeral port exhaustion once when a burst of pods pulled model weights simultaneously. If using private nodes, please add a small pre-warmed NAT with higher port allocation or use a shared egress IP pool.

alex: Autoscaler suggestion for single-GPU nodes: initial = 0, min = 0, max = 4 (for 8 pods with 2 pods/node depending on CPU/memory). Use pod priority + preemption for lower-priority jobs. Use taint key=workload:value=batch-gpu:NoSchedule. Pods get tolerations.

cheng: That sounds reasonable. For node sizes, I'm thinking n1-standard-8 with 1 GPU. Any objections?

maria: n1-standard-8 is fine. If using A10G consider n2-standard variants for better PCIe/IO, but it's not a must. Also set node auto-repair on.

alex: Example Terraform node pool snippet that worked for other regions (adjust names/zone):

```hcl
resource "google_container_node_pool" "batch_gpu" {
  name       = "batch-gpu-pool"
  cluster    = var.cluster_name
  initial_node_count = 0
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 0
    max_node_count = 4
  }
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-8"
    accelerators {
      type  = "nvidia-tesla-a10g"
      count = 1
    }
    oauth_scopes = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    metadata = {"disable-legacy-endpoints"="true"}
    tags = ["batch-gpu"]
  }
  management { auto_repair = true }
  node_taint { key = "workload" value = "batch-gpu" effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }
}
```

cheng: Nice. Re: quotas — what's a safe GPU quota to request? 4 nodes * 1 GPU = 4, but we should request room for capacity growth.

sam: Ask for 8 A10G (or equivalent T4 count if choosing T4) so we have headroom. File the quota request with GCP support and include project + region + SKU. Use the internal quota template: https://go/redwood-reqs/gpu-quota (internal link).

maria: Also add a note to the ticket about NAT IP shortage; request additional external IPs for the subnet or state intent to use Cloud NAT.

infra-bot: Deployment checklist: 1) Open quota ticket, 2) Add Terraform change in infra repo, 3) Create K8s PriorityClass for batch-gpu, 4) Add nodepool taint + node label, 5) Verify Cloud NAT config.

ops-oncall: Quick tests after provisioning: scale up to 2 nodes with a test job that pulls large model weights to confirm NAT ports and startup time. Watch kube-scheduler events for pod backoff.

cheng: Thanks all — I'll create the infra PR + quota ticket this afternoon and tag @alex for review. Will set autoscaler max=4 and request 8 GPU quota for safety.

alex: Sounds good. If you pick T4 ping me, I'll update the packing guidance. :thumbsup:
